lesson_title: Identifying a Transformation from the Coordinates of an Image
hook_text: Two GPS points. No route. She named the road from the coordinates alone.
clip_script:
A delivery company tracks its scooters on a map gridded with the depot at the origin, one block to a unit. One morning the log for a scooter shows only two entries: start at 3 semicolon 2, end at 2 semicolon negative 3. The dispatcher wants to know what happened — whether the rider took a legal shortcut or cut through the park — and she asks the learner on work experience to read the move.

The learner writes the pairs. The coordinates swapped, and the new second one changed sign: a rotation of 90 degrees clockwise about the depot. He checks: 9 plus 4 is 13 both times, so the scooter ended as far from the depot as it started. The ring road is exactly that quarter-circle. Compare, check the distance, read the pattern — and the move names itself.
visual_style: A city grid with a depot at the centre; two dots appear, a dotted quarter-circle swings between them along a ring road, and a label reads 90 degrees clockwise
call_to_action: Open the full session to name any transformation from a point and its image.
